event_name: The Happiest Hour at Agave Bandido
blurb: Agave Bandido in Dunwoody runs a Friday happy hour and they're not shy about it. Discounted appetizers, cold beers, and the kind of bold Mexican-leaning menu that makes three o'clock feel like a reasonable time to start the weekend. It's right on High Street, which means you can walk it into the rest of your Friday evening without getting back in the car. For the crowd that wraps up work early on a Friday and wants somewhere worth landing before dinner, this is a solid answer. Walk in, order something with a kick, and let the week go.
scoring_notes: Recurring happy hour, so uniqueness is low. But the Dunwoody location and adult-skewing audience make it relevant. Good filler content for a neighborhood newsletter, even if it wouldn't carry a featured slot on a strong week.

blurb: Four-week mini series, beginner friendly, Friday nights at 8. If you've ever watched swing dancing and thought 'I could probably do that,' this is your actual chance to find out. The Roswell Adult Recreation Center is running a beginner-level swing series and you don't need a partner to show up. The format is casual and the skill floor is low on purpose. It's a genuinely fun Friday night activity that isn't a bar and isn't a movie, and for couples or friends looking for something a little different to do together this month, it hits. August 7 is your entry point if you want to catch the full run.
scoring_notes: Adult-skewing activity that fits young professionals and empty nesters well. Roswell is a stretch geographically for the Perimeter audience, but the series format and beginner hook give it some appeal. Not the strongest pick but legitimate filler if needed.

event_name: FUNdamental Fridays at Spruill Center for the Arts
venue: Spruill Center for the Arts, Dunwoody
blurb: Friday nights in August don't need to cost anything to be worth your time. Spruill Center for the Arts opens its doors every Friday evening for FUNdamental Fridays, a free open studio session where you bring whatever 2D project you're working on and just... make stuff. Painting, drawing, mixed media, it doesn't matter. There's no instruction, no pressure, no performance. Just a room full of people who wanted a reason to be creative on a Friday night instead of scrolling on the couch. It's the kind of low-key evening that actually recharges you. No admission, just show up with your project and your people.
scoring_notes: Free and local, solid fit for the educated, creative-adjacent Perimeter crowd. Dunwoody location is squarely in coverage area. Recurring series hurts uniqueness, but it's genuinely useful and no-cost for a Friday night out.

blurb: If you have a kid in your house who has ever said the word 'Sonic' in a non-ironic context, this weekend is their Super Bowl. Sonic EXPO Atlanta is a full fan convention built around the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise, pulling in voice actors, game developers, artists, speed runners, and the kind of creators who built careers out of loving this thing. It's not a booth at a gaming store. It's a real convention with panels, vendors, and people who fly in for this. The Cobb Galleria location makes it easy to get to from the Perimeter, and for families with kids in the 8–16 range, this is the rare event where the kids will actually be more excited than you are. Which, honestly, is worth something.
scoring_notes: Unique event with real can't-miss energy for families with kids. The Perimeter audience skews adult, but the young families segment fits well here. Convention format means it's not happening every weekend, which boosts uniqueness score.

event_name: Social Fridays on The Green at High Street Atlanta
blurb: High Street Atlanta is doing what a good outdoor space should do in summer: putting people on a lawn with food, drinks, and live music and letting the evening figure itself out. Social Fridays on The Green runs select Fridays of the month, and this Friday is one of them. You've got bites and drinks from the partnered restaurants on site, music to set the mood, and the kind of easy, no-agenda hang that's actually hard to find on a weeknight. It's right in Dunwoody, parking is a non-issue, and there's no ticket to buy. Just show up, grab something good to eat, and enjoy August before it's over.
scoring_notes: Strong location fit for Perimeter audience. The mix of young professionals and empty nesters both land here. Recurring series is the main knock, but it's a select-Fridays format which adds a small degree of can't-miss framing.

event_name: UFC 330 at Live! at The Battery Atlanta
venue: Live! at The Battery Atlanta, Atlanta, GA
blurb:
If you're going to watch UFC 330, you might as well watch it on a 36-foot screen with surround sound that makes you feel like you're cage-side.

Live! at The Battery is doing a full fight-night setup for UFC 330 — massive screen, wall-to-wall TVs, food and drink specials, and the kind of communal atmosphere where the crowd reacts together to every big moment. It's a Saturday night, it starts at 9 PM, and it's exactly the kind of out-of-the-house experience that makes a fight night actually feel like an event rather than just watching TV.

Reserve a table ahead of time. These fill up.
scoring_notes: UFC skews younger and more male than the median East Cobb reader, but the venue and format elevate it. The Battery location is convenient for East Cobb. Lower scores across the board compared to other options but it's a real, specific event with a clear audience subset. Included as a solid option for the right segment of the readership.

blurb:
Masego is one of the most interesting live performers working right now — saxophone, production, vocals, and a genre that's somewhere between jazz, R&B, and something that doesn't have a clean name yet.

He's at the Coca-Cola Roxy on Saturday night. The Roxy is a great mid-size venue — not too big to feel disconnected, not too small to feel like a club. If you've got a college-age kid home for the summer who's been listening to him, this is an easy win. And if you haven't heard Masego before, start with "Lady Lady" and see how quickly you decide you want to go.

Saturday, August 15th at 8 PM. Get tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Masego skews younger (25-35 core fanbase) but the East Cobb audience includes parents with college-age kids who'd be interested, and the artist has enough cultural cachet to appeal to the more culturally curious 40-something reader. Lower scores than the top picks but a legitimate and specific event worth including.

event_name: Six the Musical Live! at Springs Cinema & Taphouse
venue: Springs Cinema & Taphouse, Sandy Springs, GA
blurb:
Six has been one of the most talked-about musicals of the last several years — catchy, sharp, genuinely funny, and built around six powerhouse female performances. If you haven't seen it on stage, this is a legitimately great way to experience it.

Springs Cinema is screening a live capture of the original West End cast performing at London's Vaudeville Theatre, and the lineup is exactly what made the show famous in the first place. Jarneia Richard-Noel, Millie O'Connell, and the full cast bring Henry VIII's six wives into the 21st century with pop songs, sass, and the kind of energy that makes this show work. It's infectious.

Springs Cinema & Taphouse also means you can order food and drinks and watch it like an event rather than just a movie. Saturday at 4 PM in Sandy Springs — this one is especially worth it if you've got a teen or college-age kid who'd be into it. Good excuse to go together.
scoring_notes: Six skews younger but the East Cobb readership has a lot of families with teen and college-age kids, which opens this up. The taphouse format elevates it beyond a standard movie screening. The West End cast reunion makes it a one-time special screening rather than a regular showing. Good middle-ground pick.

event_name: Atlanta Braves vs. New York Mets
blurb:
The Mets are in town, and if you need a reason to get out to Truist Park this week, that's a pretty good one.

Atlanta hosts New York for a three-game series Monday through Wednesday, all with 7:15 PM first pitches. Truist Park is one of the best baseball experiences in the country — easy in, great food options, and a ballpark that feels designed for the exact kind of crowd that fills it on a summer weeknight. Whether you've got teenagers who want to get out of the house or you're just looking for a reason to sit outside with a cold drink and watch some baseball, this works.

Mets fans travel well, which means the energy in the stands is going to be there. Grab tickets before the series starts.
scoring_notes: Baseball at Truist Park is a perennial strong fit for East Cobb's family-oriented, higher-income audience. The Mets are a marquee opponent that creates genuine buzz. Weeknight games may limit turnout slightly but still worth featuring given proximity and broad appeal. Lower uniqueness score because it's a standard regular-season series.

blurb:
Most people who've been to a hundred Braves games have never stood in the dugout after dark.

The Moonlight Tours at Truist Park are a behind-the-scenes guided experience that takes you places you don't get to go on a normal game night — the press box with a beer in hand, the dugout under the moon and stars, and a backstage look at the Blue Moon Brewery inside the park. The tour includes drinks throughout and a guided walkthrough of the brewing setup with an insider from Molson Coors. It's 21+ and runs from 6 to 8 PM.

This is genuinely one of those experiences that is more fun to tell people about afterward than most things you'll do this month. "We did a nighttime dugout tour at Truist" is a better dinner conversation than almost anything else on this list. Reserve your spot before it fills up.
scoring_notes: The 21+ requirement and adult-experience framing makes this a strong empty nester pick. The novelty of a behind-the-scenes ballpark tour with drinks is high. East Cobb's income level means the ticket price is a non-issue. Thursday date is slightly limiting but the experience is unique enough to feature.

event_name: Silent Film at The Strand: Sunrise (1927)
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta, GA
blurb:
You don't have to be a film history buff to walk out of this one feeling like you saw something genuinely special.

The Strand is screening Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans, the 1927 silent film masterpiece that is still considered one of the most visually stunning movies ever made. A farmer, a city woman, a wife, and a choice that pulls him apart — the story is simple but the filmmaking is extraordinary. What makes this screening different is the live accompaniment. Ron Carter, the Strand's own House Organist and one of the most accomplished silent film accompanists in the Southeast, performs live throughout. The organ does what the soundtrack can't in a silent film — it carries the emotional weight of every scene.

This is a RARE kind of afternoon. A 100-year-old film, a live performance, a beautiful historic theater. Sunday at 3 PM. Even if you've never sought out a silent film before, this is the kind of thing worth trying once.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness — live organ accompaniment to a 100-year-old masterpiece in a historic theater is genuinely not something you can do any weekend. The educated, culturally engaged East Cobb demographic is exactly right for this. Skews toward empty nesters more than families with kids, but the 3 PM Sunday slot works well for that crowd.

event_name: Music on the Hill: Piano Man vs. Rocket Man
time: TBD (check event page for start time)
venue: Roswell City Hall, 38 Hill St, Roswell, GA
blurb:
Picture this: a blanket on the lawn, a bottle of wine, the sun going down, and two of the greatest piano-driven catalogs in rock history filling the air at the same time.

Roswell's Music on the Hill series is bringing back one of its best concepts this summer as part of the America250 celebration. Mark Kovaly and Daniel Deal face off in a "Piano Man vs. Rocket Man" tribute show, trading songs from Billy Joel and Elton John all night long. We're talking "Piano Man," "Tiny Dancer," "Scenes from an Italian Restaurant," "Rocket Man" — the kind of songs that every person at this event already knows every word to.

This is a free, outdoor concert on the lawn at Roswell City Hall. Bring a chair or a blanket, pack a cooler, and make a whole evening of it. There's no ticket to buy and no reason not to go. Get there early if you want a good spot on the grass.
scoring_notes: Billy Joel and Elton John are quintessential for the 40-55 age bracket that dominates this readership. Free outdoor concert removes all friction. The America250 tie-in gives it a one-time-special feel. Families and empty nesters both fit. Strong overall pick for East Cobb.

event_name: Strand Ole Opry: The Sounds of Simon & Garfunkel
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta, GA
blurb:
If you grew up with "Bridge Over Troubled Water" on the radio or "Mrs. Robinson" on a road trip soundtrack, Saturday night at the Strand is going to hit different.

The Strand Ole Opry is putting their own spin on Simon & Garfunkel's catalog this weekend, and the format is genuinely worth showing up for. A full bluegrass band backs a cast of local singers as they work through the classics — the harmonies, the storytelling, the songs that feel like they were written for a quieter, more intentional version of life. Reimagining folk-pop legends through a bluegrass lens is an unexpected combination that actually makes a lot of sense once you hear it.

The Strand is a beautiful old theater right on Marietta Square. It's the kind of night where you grab dinner nearby first, walk over, and let the music do the rest. Saturday, August 15th at 8 PM.
scoring_notes: Simon and Garfunkel are deeply resonant for the 40-55+ crowd. The bluegrass-band twist makes this a unique version of the material rather than a standard tribute show. The Strand is right in the heart of East Cobb's backyard. Strong fit for both empty nesters and established families looking for a date night.

venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta Square
blurb:
Film festivals don't usually come this close to home, and this one is legitimately worth your attention. The Cobb International Film Festival runs at the Strand Theatre on Marietta Square and showcases feature films, shorts, and documentaries from filmmakers at every level, pulled from all over the world.

What makes it different from a typical movie night is the conversation after the screenings. Several films end with a Q&A with the filmmaker, which gives you context you just don't get sitting in a multiplex. It's the kind of event you walk out of with something to actually talk about.

Marietta Square is the backdrop, so dinner before or drinks after is an easy add. This one kicks off Thursday, August 6, which means you can build a whole evening around it right at the start of the week.
scoring_notes: A film festival with an international scope sits well with an educated, higher-income East Cobb audience. The Marietta Square venue is walkable and familiar territory for this crowd. Filmmaker Q&As are a genuine differentiator. Scores slightly lower on audience match because the content is adult-leaning and less relevant to the family-with-teens segment.
